title: Wrestling: shots, sprawls, and scoring
note: A takedown starts with a level change, dropping the hips, and a penetration step that drives through the opponent. The defense is the sprawl. Under United World Wrestling rules, freestyle allows leg attacks while Greco-Roman forbids holds below the waist; a fall or a big enough lead ends the bout early.

read.title: The shot and the sprawl
text: Most takedowns begin before contact. The attacker changes levels, bending the knees and dropping the hips while keeping the back straight and the head up. From that low position a penetration step carries the hips in under the opponent, so the drive comes from the legs rather than the arms. A double-leg attacks both legs at once; a single-leg isolates one.

The answer to the shot is the sprawl. The defender throws the legs back and drops the hips onto the attacker's head and shoulders. Taking the legs out of reach removes the target, and the defender's weight now presses down on the shooter.

International wrestling runs on United World Wrestling rules. Freestyle, used for men and women, allows leg attacks. Greco-Roman forbids holds below the waist and active use of the legs, so it rewards upper-body throws and lifts. A senior bout lasts two three-minute periods. It ends early with a fall, both shoulders clearly controlled on the mat, or with technical superiority, a lead of 10 points in freestyle or 8 in Greco-Roman.
